title: A Unified Protocol for Arbitrary Z Rotations of a Class of Bosonic cQED Qubits
abstract: Bosonic-qubit encodings provide diverse approaches to storing and processing quantum information, with logical operations often implemented through encoding-specific physical strategies. Here, we identify a class of bosonic Fock-based qubits in circuit QED for which distinct implementations of arbitrary Z rotations share a common structure. We formulate this structure as a six-step protocol that provides a unified procedure for implementing arbitrary Z rotations across this class of bosonic cQED qubits. The applicability of the protocol is determined by a specific condition on the encoding, providing a criterion for identifying bosonic Fock-based cQED qubits that admit the common implementation.
summary: This paper introduces a unified, six-step protocol for performing arbitrary Z rotations on a broad class of bosonic cQED qubits. The protocol's applicability is determined by a specific mathematical condition related to the qubit's encoding structure. It is significant because it provides a systematic tool to analyze and control quantum gates across various physical implementations in circuit QED.
main_problem: To develop a unified, systematic protocol for implementing arbitrary Z rotations on a diverse class of bosonic cQED qubits.
main_result: A six-step protocol is formulated that successfully implements the Z(theta) rotation for any bosonic Fock-based cQED qubit satisfying a specific mathematical condition derived from the encoding.
method: The protocol is derived by analyzing the required sequence of dispersive and Rabi interactions necessary to engineer the relative phase between logical states.
model_or_system: The system involves bosonic cQED qubits, modeled using a dispersive Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{dis}$) and a Rabi Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{Rabi}$), realized in circuit QED architectures.
key_observables: The successful implementation of the Z(theta) rotation operator, and the mathematical condition governing the applicability of the protocol.
important_parameters: The coupling strength ($\chi$), the Rabi frequency ($\Omega_d(t)$), and the specific structure of the qubit encoding defined by GCDs of photon numbers.
main_assumptions: The protocol is only guaranteed to work for qubits satisfying the condition that the difference between certain photon number indices ($m' - n'$) is odd.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the general problem of implementing Z rotations across different bosonic qubit encodings. It then derives the six-step protocol based on Hamiltonian engineering. Finally, it rigorously tests the protocol's applicability by analyzing various known qubit types (Cat, Binomial, Dual-rail) against the necessary mathematical condition.
why_interesting: This work provides a general theoretical framework for controlling quantum gates in superconducting circuits, unifying disparate physical implementations under a single mathematical protocol.
